name: Financial Assistance for Education of the Wards of Beedi/Cine/IOMC/LSDM Workers (Pre-Matric)

raw.catalogue_text: Financial Assistance for Education of the Wards of Beedi/Cine/IOMC/LSDM Workers (Pre-Matric) | Provider: Labour Welfare Organisation | Academic Year: 2026-27 | Type: Labour Welfare / Industrial Wards | Open: 2026-06-01 | Close: 2026-10-31
raw.specification_text:
Scheme Name: Financial Assistance for Education of the Wards of Beedi/Cine/IOMC/LSDM Workers (Pre-Matric)
Ministry: Ministry of Labour and Employment
Department: Labour Welfare Organisation
Target Classes: Class 1, Class 2, Class 3, Class 4, Class 5, Class 6, Class 7, Class 8, Class 9, Class 10
Academic Requirement: Passed previous year examination on first attempt and enrolled in a recognized school.
School Type Requirement: 
Annual Income Ceiling: Rs. 120000
Selection Mode: Direct / Merit
Financial Assistance: For Class 9 and 10 students: ₹2,000 per annum (Class 1-4: ₹1,000, Class 5-8: ₹1,500). - Rs. 2000 per annum
Registration Requirement: One Time Registration (OTR) with Aadhaar/EID on NSP
raw.faq_text:
Q: Who can apply for Financial Assistance for Education of the Wards of Beedi/Cine/IOMC/LSDM Workers (Pre-Matric)?
A: Eligible students studying in Class 1, Class 2, Class 3, Class 4, Class 5, Class 6, Class 7, Class 8, Class 9, Class 10.
Q: What is the official portal?
A: https://scholarships.gov.in
Q: Is OTR required for AY 2026-27?
A: Yes, One Time Registration is mandatory on National Scholarship Portal.

eligibility_summary.occupational_requirement: At least one parent must be an active worker in Beedi, Cine, Iron Ore/Manganese Ore/Chrome Ore (IOMC), or Limestone and Dolomite Mines (LSDM) with at least 6 months of continuous service.
eligibility_summary.academic_requirement: Passed previous year examination on first attempt and enrolled in a recognized school.

benefits_summary.details: For Class 9 and 10 students: ₹2,000 per annum (Class 1-4: ₹1,000, Class 5-8: ₹1,500).

raw.inclusion_rationale: Direct financial aid scheme specifically for children of unorganized mine and factory workers attending secondary school (Classes 9 and 10).
